item.title: Re: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hello again! how are you doing?

Thanks for the response, especially the bit about the ending.

The ending definitely does need something more than just lost hope. I like bleak endings, but they only really work when there's a lesson learned, or if it affects more than just the main character. Right now, it seems like the ending doesn't have a payoff and only affects the main character, which thankfully you helped bring to my attention. I think as you recommended, the ending should be bittersweet instead of bleak.
I started to brainstorm a different idea for the ending:
Instead of just all hope being lost and he transforms, The Oneiroi Collective gives him an offer: he can be placed in an endless dream, which would replicate reality completely, with one catch: it takes place only in the summer of 1965, and only in his home town. With no other option, Ty takes the offer, leaving his physical body (which now completely transforms into an instance of the SCP) behind. He falls asleep for the last time.

Of course, I'll probably brainstorm more ending ideas that may work better.

Thanks again for the critique, and I hope you have had a merry Christmas and a great day.

Sincerely, Gravy.

item.title: Re: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hey! How are you doing?

Thank you so much for the response.

The ending is bleak, and I definitely think it could use some work. I'm considering adding something to the ending, to make it bittersweet (like Caspian2 recommended). Instead of Ty just transforming completely, basically making him brain dead, he is offered to order a dream that lasts forever. A dream that replicates real life. However, it will always be the summer of 1965, and his physical body will be completely transformed. With no other option, Ty accepts the offer, and he falls asleep for the last time.
Of course, this is just an idea, and I'll probably brainstorm other endings that might work better.

The reason he knows who The Oneiroi Collective are is more simple. Whenever anyone picks up the phone on SCP-1498, someone claiming to be from The Oneiroi Collective will answer the call.
The reason he finds anomalous abilities is slightly more complex. Ty's main flaw as a character is that he's driven by boredom, and nothing else. All his actions at the beginning of the tale are taken without consideration, as he only takes those actions to relieve himself of boredom. So, when he finds the SCP, although he's at first startled, he eventually becomes enthralled and starts to inspect it, eventually using the phone, in which the main plot begins. He gets addicted to using the SCP not only because it's one of its anomalous abilities, but also because it seems to be a way to escape the boredom of his mind. Of course, he gets more than he bargains for.
If you're asking why he thinks that it's the SCP causing the changes to his body, it's more or less a hopeful guess on his part. He makes the connection between the phone related changes to the phone related sheep and assumes that it's the SCP causing the issues (which, he is correct). As usual, this detail could be ironed out more.

Again, thanks for responding. I think I'm going to start writing the draft. When that's finished and edited, I'll submit it to the draft critique forum and probably PM you.

Have a great day, and I hope you had a merry Christmas!

Sincerely, Gravy.

I think this shows promise, and like Caspian2, I definitely think the ending is a bit vague… but I also know that devising a plot and then building towards an ending is rarely complete at this stage.

The way you've laid out the story tells me you understand how stories work and I am convinced this would work if executed well. GREENLIGHT

One thing, why would this kid know what the Oneroi West was? He found the SCP in the woods right? So why would he be clued into things that are anomalous?

item.title: Re: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there gravyismad. So I'm close to a greenlight for this, mainly because you've chosen to base your Tale on an existing SCP and the way you've outlined your story clearly shows you've given it some thought.

My only concern right now is the ending. Could you elaborate a bit more on how you want the story to end? At the moment, it sounds bleak: he comes to the realisation that there's no hope? And then what? Ideally, there should be some kind of bittersweetness to an ending: he gains something, but at the cost of something else.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
A troublesome teenager utilizes mysterious livestock to control his dreams. A tale about SCP-1498.

Seeking Greenlight: Recieved

Page Type: Tale

This tale doesn't take place in The Foundation itself. It's based around one specific SCP before it was contained.

Elevator Pitch: A teenager by the name of Ty encounters SCP-1498 in the woods, and begins to abuse its abilities. However, when he slowly starts to become an instance of SCP-1498, he struggles to find help. This takes place a month before SCP-1498's original containment date.

Central Narrative: Taking place in august of 1965, just before SCP-1498 (which this tale is about) is contained, a troublesome teenager, Ty, stumbles across SCP-1498 in the woods and learns that he can order dreams from the SCP. He begins to abuse the ability, spending most of his time asleep, dreaming. However, when his body begins to slowly turn into instances of the SCP, he attempts to find "The Oneiroi Collective" (the people who possibly designed the SCP) to help him. However, upon searching phone books, he discovers that the phone number to call them only exists on the instances of SCP-1498. He hurries back to where he last saw them, but they've vanished completely. Luckily, a phone wire that goes through the woods leads him to an abandoned office building, where he finds the livestock entering. Ty catches up to them, managing to get on the phone with The Oneiroi Collective. However, it's too late, and Ty completely transforms into an instance of SCP-1498-1, mindlessly wandering back into the woods, ironically dreaming of the days when he didn't dream at all.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The realization that Ty basically has no way out of the situation he's in. This is the foundation of most of the tension throughout the tale, as it will seem almost completely hopeless. Which, by the end, it's revealed that it was, indeed, hopeless. At least, that's the goal I'll try to achieve with this tale.

Additional Notes: Obviously, this is a rough outline of what happens, and it will almost certainly change (hopefully for the better) as critiques come in. I'm also not the author of SCP-1498, and as so tried to keep this story as distant from the lore set up in the SCP itself.

Here's a link to SCP-1498, which this tale is based on: http://www.scpwiki.com/scp-1498
P.S, thanks for the tip Zyn, I'll take note of that
